Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-25

Duration: ~50 minutes
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Aisha Kapoor (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (BrightWave CTO), Maya Li (BrightWave ML Eng), Sophie Nguyen (BrightWave Security), Tom Rivera (BrightWave Product)

Summary (auto-gen - may be rough):
Redwood Optimize walkthrough focusing on quantization profiles (INT8 vs FP8). Discussed quality vs latency tradeoffs, recommendations for BrightWave's clinical summarization workload, security/compliance questions (KMS, audit logs, SOC2), and next steps: run regression tests on BrightWave prompts, share benchmarks and pricing, and schedule pilot for Dedicated capacity.

00:00 Liam: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, yeah were going to run through the Optimize module specifically quantization profiles, right, INT8 and FP8 and how they trade off latency and quality. Aisha is our SE, shell lead the technical bits.
00:18 Aisha: Hi all, thanks Raj, Maya, Sophie. Quick agenda: overview, demo of the console Optimize tab, show the INT8/FP8 profiles, then quality vs latency charts, and finish with recommendations for your summarization workload.
00:35 Raj: Sounds good. Quick context - we have a clinical notes summarization pipeline, 1.2k requests per minute at peak, 95th pct latency target is 200ms/token, and our quality bar is pretty high because downstream decisions are clinical. Were evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private.
00:55 Tom: timeline is Q3 pilot, Q4 production. Cost is a big factor but cannot degrade patient-facing quality.
01:10 Aisha: Understood. Two things matter here: token latency and model degradation from quant. INT8 gives big cost wins but sometimes small quality regressions; FP8 is sort of mid-ground depending on hardware kernels.
01:30 Maya: Can you explain how Redwood chooses kernels? We use a mix of sequence lengths, typical note is 1-2k tokens.
01:45 Aisha: Sure. The runtime probes model architecture and sequence-length distribution and picks optimized attention and matmul kernels; for quantization we pick per-layer scaling and symmetric/asymmetric schemes. In practice for long-form notes INT8 prefix caching helps a lot so you often see better amortized latency.
02:10 Sophie: Security question, if we run Dedicated or Private, how is KMS handled? We need HSM-backed keys and audit logs for every inference.
02:25 Liam: For Dedicated we integrate with your cloud KMS (and HSM via partner integrations). Private on-prem supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and audit logs. Well share the security pack after the call.
02:40 Maya: Cool. Demo please.
03:00 Aisha: (screen share) Heres the Redwood Console > Optimize tab. You can pick a model and then choose quant profiles - we have baseline FP16, INT8-compat, FP8-high, and a few hybrid profiles. This example shows GPTx-7B-fp16 baseline vs int8-quant and fp8-quant.
03:35 Aisha: Now we run a small batch of your prompt set (I uploaded a 200-example subset). On the right you can see Quality delta (BLEU/ROUGE proxies + our semantic similarity score) and latency histogram.
03:55 Aisha: For this workload, INT8 reduced per-token latency by ~28% and cost by ~45% but quality delta median is -0.8% relative to FP16 on our semantic metric. FP8 reduced latency by ~15% and cost by ~25% with median quality delta -0.2%. Theres tail behavior though, see 95th pct where FP8 preserves more.
04:30 Raj: Those numbers are promising but that 0.8% drop worries me. Do you have qualitative examples where INT8 fails?
04:45 Aisha: Yes; some rare numeric tables and very long parenthetical notes show hallucination or tokenization drift in INT8. Ill paste sample diffs in the benchmark sheet.
05:00 Maya: How reproducible are these deltas across models? We sometimes switch model variants.
05:15 Aisha: Reproducibility depends on architecture. For decoder-only LLMs with stable layer norms INT8 is usually safe; for some fused-attention architectures FP8 is gentler. Our Optimize tool runs per-model profiling and flags risky tensors.
05:40 Tom: If we go Dedicated, can we pin a profile per route? We want API endpoints for patient-facing summarization to use FP8 and internal batch jobs INT8.
05:55 Liam: Absolutely; per-route model + quant profile routing is supported. You can do policy based routing too for latency/cost tiers.
06:10 Sophie: On compliance, do you provide audit logs for which profile and model was used for an inference? We need traceability for audits.
06:25 Aisha: Yes, every request logs model_id, profile_id, kernel_id, node id and the routing decision, and we store that in the audit log. For Private deployments logs can be shipped to your SIEM.
06:45 Raj: Can we run A/B tests with automatic fallback? For example, if INT8 degrades on a subset, fall back to FP8 or FP16.
07:00 Aisha: Yes. Rollouts in Console support canary, A/B, and automatic rollback if quality metrics degrade past thresholds you set. We can tie it to your eval set.
07:20 Speaker 1 (transcription artifact): mm-hmm uh yeah
07:30 Aisha: (shows chart) Heres the quality vs latency curve. Note the Pareto frontier - you can pick a sweet spot. For BrightWaves notes we recommend FP8-high profile for patient-facing paths and INT8-safeguarded profile for background batch.
08:05 Maya: Will that require re-training or fine-tuning?
08:15 Aisha: Generally no. Quant-aware finetuning can help but usually our per-layer calibration and per-token bias compensation reduces regression without retraining. We offer optional QAT pass if you want to push further.
08:40 Raj: What about operator visibility? Our Platform team needs dashboards for cost by route.
08:50 Liam: Redwood Console shows token-level cost and latency per-route, and you can export hourly cost reports. Well send you a sample export.
09:05 Tom: How about throughput under burst? If we pick FP8 on Dedicated, can we guarantee 95th latency under spikes?
09:20 Aisha: Dedicated has configurable autoscaling with burst pools. For strict SLOs we size a baseline reserved capacity and a burst buffer. The runtime also does smart batching; that helps throughput but careful with latency-sensitive calls - we can set a low batching window.
09:50 Maya: Any real-world numbers for long sequences?
10:00 Aisha: For 1-2k tokens we see INT8 throughput increase of ~1.6x on A100-class and FP8 around 1.25x; 95th latency improvements vary with batching and cache hit rate.
10:20 Raj: Competitors like Anthropic said they avoid INT8 in clinical. How do you mitigate risk?
10:35 Aisha: Were explicit about which layers are quantized, run targeted regression tests on your prompt set, and provide automated rollbacks. For high-risk routes we recommend FP8 or keep FP16.
10:55 Sophie: Data residency: our notes must stay in the customer VPC. If we do Hosted, is that possible?
11:10 Liam: Hosted API stores limited metadata; for full VPC isolation youd want Dedicated or Private. Hosted can be region-restricted but not VPC-isolated.
11:30 Maya: Ok. Can you share the benchmark spreadsheet and the per-sentence diffs?
11:40 Liam: Yep, heres the link to the benchmark doc: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/brightwave-int8-vs-fp8 and the security pack: https://redwood.ai/security/brightwave-pack. Ill also upload the diffs and example failures to the drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/brightwave-samples
12:05 Raj: On pricing, whats the delta for FP8 vs INT8 vs FP16?
12:15 Liam: Roughly INT8 is ~45% cheaper than FP16 for token compute; FP8 is ~25% cheaper. Dedicated reserved pricing has additional discounts. Ill send a detailed pricing sheet.
12:35 Tom: For the pilot, can we start with a small Dedicated pool with FP8 for prod-similar traffic and INT8 for batch?
12:50 Aisha: Yes, we can set up two routes and split traffic. We can also run the regression test nightly and alert if quality drifts.
13:10 Maya: One more question: how does prefix/KV cache work with quant profiles? Any incompatibilities?
13:25 Aisha: KV cache is independent of quant profile; we quantize activations/kernels, the cache stores keys/values in the runtime format. Some profiles have slight precision differences but cache hits remain compatible. If you switch profiles mid-session theres an incompatibility so we avoid switching for open sessions.
13:50 Raj: Great. Next steps recap?
14:00 Liam: Recap: 1) Aisha will run the full BrightWave prompt set comparison INT8 vs FP8 and provide per-sample diffs (due 2026-05-02). 2) Raj to share anonymized traces by 2026-04-30. 3) Liam to send pricing + Dedicated pilot terms by 2026-04-27. 4) Schedule follow-up technical deep dive for private deployment/KMS - suggest week of 2026-05-04.
14:30 Sophie: Please include SOC2/ISO attestation and KMS/HSM integration docs.
14:40 Liam: Will do.

14:55 Aisha: Thanks all, well follow up with the spreadsheet and the sample diffs.
